cover.headline: A ticketing monopoly at 22x earnings: cheap against its own history, but growth now comes from low-margin catering and the owner sets the price
cover.lead: IRCTC is the Railways' 62.4%-government-owned sole online ticket seller (89% of reserved tickets), its mandated caterer, its bottled-water supplier (Rail Neer) and a pilgrimage-train operator. Q1FY27 revenue rose 18% on catering (+34%), but EBITDA fell 2.7% as ticketing stalled (+0.6%) and one-off costs hit. We forecast EPS of ₹18.0 / ₹19.8 / ₹21.5 for FY27-29E, 2-3% below PL (14-Aug-2026). The street values IRCTC on **P/E** (PL 35x FY28E; Choice 25x the FY28-29E average). On the house rule we start from its own one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 (42.7x) and apply the sector move of the only five comparable names with a five-year P/E history: the internet platforms brokers group it with (Info Edge, IndiaMART) and the railway-PSU service companies the market trades it with (Container Corp, RailTel, RITES), median −26%. **31.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹20.7 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY.** The peer set matters: with no sector move the value is ₹880, with the internet platforms' move alone (−48%) ₹450, and the DCF (Ke 11.9%) gives only ₹411. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The ticketing monopoly is a cash machine that has stopped growing
arguments.p: Internet ticketing earned ~75% of segment profit in FY26 at an 82% margin on ₹1,536 cr of revenue. But revenue rose only 0.6% in Q1FY27: the convenience fee (₹10/₹20 per ticket on UPI) has not risen for about seven years, UPI is now 51% of tickets, and non-fee income fell 8% after ads were removed and agents curbed. Management targets ~7% growth; we assume 4% then 6%, with no fee rise.

arguments.h: Growth now comes from catering, at a tenth of the margin
arguments.p: Catering grew 13% in FY26 and 34% in Q1FY27 (prepaid Vande Bharat trains, licence fees, e-catering, election specials) and is 53% of Q1 revenue, but earns a 9-12% segment margin; prepaid trains pay 5% GST without input credit. Tourism (+19% in FY26) and Rail Neer (capacity-bound) are also low-margin. So the EBITDA margin fell from 36% (FY23) to 32% (FY26) and 28% (Q1FY27); we expect ~29%.

arguments.h: The owner is also the regulator, the customer and a seller
arguments.p: The Railways set the convenience fee, catering prices and licence terms, owe IRCTC ₹1,882 cr, run a rival app front-end (RailOne) and in Oct-2021 ordered a 50% fee share (withdrawn the next day). The government plans a ~5% OFS in FY27 (merchant bankers appointed) and the CMD post has been on additional charge since Jul-2026.

arguments.h: Valuation: the price has de-rated to half its own history
arguments.p: At ₹455 IRCTC trades at 25.2x FY27E and 22.0x Sep-28E EPS, against a 42.7x forward median since 2021; foreign funds cut their stake from 7.2% to 3.9% in six months. Platform peers de-rated as much (Info Edge −38%, IndiaMART −59% vs five-year medians). The DCF at ₹411 says today's price is not obviously cheap on cash flows: the upside is about sentiment and the multiple, not about earnings.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): catering growth without election specials, ticketing margin with the disaster-recovery spend, Rail Neer resin costs.
Government OFS of ~5% in FY27 (merchant bankers appointed; floor price and dates not announced by 30-Sep-2026): a supply overhang until it is done.
Appointment of a regular CMD (charge held by the Director, Tourism & Marketing since Jul-2026).
RBI decision on the iPay payment-aggregator licence (final application filed by the 4-Aug-2026 deadline; response expected within FY27) and the full launch of the new website.
Any Ministry decision on the convenience fee (unchanged for about seven years) or catering tariffs (last raised in 2019, per an analyst): the largest swing factor in either direction.

sections.title: Four businesses granted by one owner: tickets, food, water and pilgrim trains

blocks.p: IRCTC is a Navratna central public-sector enterprise under the Ministry of Railways, 62.4% owned by the Government of India. Almost everything it does depends on a mandate from the Railways. **Internet ticketing**: it is the only authorised online seller of reserved railway tickets and earns a convenience fee per e-ticket (₹10 non-AC / ₹20 AC when paid by UPI, ₹15 / ₹30 by card) plus advertising, agent, payment-gateway and loyalty income. **Catering**: under the 2017 catering policy it runs food on trains and at stations, mostly by licensing the work to private caterers; on prepaid trains (Vande Bharat, Rajdhani, Shatabdi) food is in the fare and IRCTC books the turnover. **Rail Neer**: packaged drinking water at ₹14 a bottle from its own and PPP plants (15 operational in FY22), with profit shared with the Railways. **Tourism**: Bharat Gaurav and state pilgrimage (State Teertha) trains, luxury trains, two Tejas Express trains, packages and air/hotel booking.

sections.title: From a railway department to a listed monopoly: IPO, Covid, two OFS sales and one fee scare

blocks.p: IRCTC was set up in 1999 to take catering, tourism and online ticketing out of the Railways. The government sold 12.6% in the Oct-2019 IPO, 20% in Dec-2020 and 5% in Dec-2022, and plans ~5% more in FY27. Each sale and each policy move mattered more to the share price than the quarterly numbers: the stock rose ~17x from its split-adjusted IPO price (₹64) to its Oct-2021 peak (~₹1,100), fell ~29% intraday when the Railways ordered a fee share, and has de-rated steadily since FY25.

sections.title: Rail travel grows ~8% a year; online booking is already saturated; the money is in what passengers eat and where they go

blocks.p: Indian Railways carries the passengers; IRCTC sells ~89% of reserved tickets online (13.27 crore tickets in Q1FY27, 14.58 lakh a day; share 88.92% vs 88.78%). Of daily bookings ~53-54% come through the RailConnect app, ~17% the website and ~28% business associates (OTAs such as MakeMyTrip, ixigo); G2G bookings for defence forces are the rest (Q1FY27 call). Management cites ~8% year-on-year passenger growth (Q1FY27 call). New premium capacity: Vande Bharat chair-car trains (81 catered by IRCTC) and ~20 Vande Bharat sleeper trains expected over the next year.

bullets: **RailOne.** RailOne, the Railways' own super-app (built by CRIS), sells reserved, unreserved and platform tickets but books reserved tickets through IRCTC's system; management saw 'some diversion' of non-convenience income (Q1FY27 call).

**Catering.** Catering prices are administered by the Ministry of Railways (last revised in 2019, PL Q4 call question); opt-out of meals on prepaid trains is ~25-30%; e-catering ~1.7 lakh meals a day; branded players and centralised kitchens under discussion.

**Travel and pilgrimage.** Choice (23-Sep-2026) groups IRCTC with travel platforms (ixigo, TBO Tek, RateGain): online travel penetration rising to 46% by FY27E; domestic travel 86% of tourism spend; Bharat Gaurav trains ~40% of IRCTC tourism revenue.

**Payments.** UPI is now 51% of IRCTC tickets (48.7% a year earlier). It is cheaper for passengers, so each shift lowers the fee IRCTC earns per ticket; iPay is IRCTC's attempt to keep payment economics in-house.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** the tailwind is real and IRCTC is its gatekeeper, but it reaches the low-margin businesses. From FY23 to FY26 segment revenue grew +47% while segment profit before exceptional items grew +32%; ticketing, the high-margin part, grew +28%. Unless the Railways raise the fee, more travel mostly means more catering turnover.

sections.title: Internet ticketing: an 80%-margin monopoly whose price is set by its owner, and whose volume is already maxed out

blocks.p: IRCTC sold 13.27 crore tickets in Q1FY27 and took 88.9% of reserved railway bookings. The segment earned ₹1,536 cr in FY26 (+7.7%) at an 81.8% segment margin before exceptional items. About two-thirds is the convenience fee (₹248 cr in Q1FY27, +5%); the rest is advertising, agent fees, payment-gateway and loyalty income (₹113 cr, −8%). Three things cap growth: (1) **volume** grows only with reserved seats, and almost all are already booked online; (2) **price**: the fee (₹10/₹20 on UPI, ₹15/₹30 on cards) has not risen for about seven years (investor on the Q1FY27 call), and management will not "announce anything" until "it will pinch us"; (3) **mix**: UPI rose to 51% of tickets. Q1FY27 revenue grew 0.6%; an investor on the call noted it had barely grown for eight quarters.

pair.title: Segment margin: 84-85% at best, 76-80% in the last two quarters

bullets: **Margin pressure is partly self-inflicted and partly one-off.** Q4FY26 carried ₹17 cr of CSR and ₹8 cr of higher direct costs; Q1FY27 carried ₹10 cr of platform maintenance. The NGET hardware and software refresh (~₹150 cr invested; target capacity above 1 lakh tickets a minute from ~37,000) and an active-active disaster-recovery site at Secunderabad will add cost through FY27. Management's range is 80-85%.

**Non-fee income fell for reasons IRCTC chose.** The new website (beta from 15-Jul-2026) has no ads, captcha or pop-ups; agents were restricted at peak booking hours; RailOne diverted some traffic. Management wants to get back to ₹150 cr a quarter via iPay, e-wallet loyalty (four banks) and a unified travel portal.

**Our forecast:** +4% in FY27E and +6% a year after, margin 80-80.5%, no fee increase: ₹1,597 / ₹1,693 / ₹1,794 cr. A 10% higher fee on all tickets would add ~₹100 cr of revenue and ~₹75 cr of net profit (~5% of EPS); a 50% fee share with the Railways (the Oct-2021 order) would remove ~₹500 cr of revenue and roughly a quarter of EPS.

sections.title: Catering: the growth engine, at a tenth of ticketing's margin

blocks.p: Catering revenue was ₹2,399 cr in FY26 (+12.9%) and ₹732 cr in Q1FY27 (+33.9%). Management broke down Q1: onboard sales on prepaid trains ₹413 cr (₹301 cr a year earlier), licence fees from mobile units ₹224 cr (₹192 cr), static units ₹33 cr (₹20 cr), e-catering licence fees ₹22 cr (₹9 cr), election specials ₹41 cr (₹5 cr; state elections, will not recur in Q2). The model is mostly licensing: IRCTC tenders trains and stalls to caterers and earns a fee; on prepaid trains it books the full turnover, pays the caterer (₹222 per Vande Bharat meal in the example given) and pays 5% GST without input credit, so margins there are thinner. The segment margin was 10.4% in FY26 and 9.3% in Q1FY27 (₹10 cr of HR cost and ₹4 cr of proof-of-concept trains).

pair.title: Margin: 12-14% a year ago, 6-10% in the last two quarters
pair.source: Quarterly segment results (Q4FY26: ECL ₹16 cr, CSR ₹5 cr; Q1FY27: HR ₹10 cr, POC ₹4 cr)

bullets: **Drivers:** ~20 Vande Bharat sleeper trains over the next year (~₹6 cr of licence fee each, ~₹120 cr in total), ~8% passenger growth, e-catering (1.25 lakh to 1.69 lakh meals a day) and e-pantry ordering on 50+ trains (target ~100).

**Constraints:** menu prices are administered by the Ministry (last raised in 2019, per an analyst on the Q4FY26 call); 25-30% of prepaid passengers opt out of meals; quality complaints keep branded caterers and centralised kitchens on the agenda; licence-fee enhancement under the CC-60 policy is in court.
**Our forecast:** +19% in FY27E (Q2-Q4 ~+14% after Q1's +34%), +13% and +12% after; margin 10.0% then 10.5%: ₹2,855 / ₹3,226 / ₹3,613 cr of revenue, ₹285 / ₹339 / ₹379 cr of segment profit.

sections.title: Tourism and Rail Neer: growing, seasonal, capacity-bound and low-margin

blocks.p: **Tourism** (including State Teertha pilgrimage trains) earned ₹890 cr in FY26 (+19.5%) at a 13.6% margin before exceptional items; Q1 is the weak quarter (₹168 cr, 11.5%) and Q3-Q4 the strong ones (16-19%). Management expects more than ₹1,000 cr in FY27. Bharat Gaurav trains are ~40% of the segment (Choice); two Tejas Express trains are run as corporate trains and have weaker margins (Q4FY26 call), but the first Tejas naming-rights deal was signed in Aug-2026. We assume +15% / +14% / +12% at a 13.5% margin.

**Rail Neer** earned ₹408 cr gross in FY26 (₹391 cr after sales to IRCTC's own catering) at a 13.6% margin. It is bound by capacity: 17.77 lakh bottles a day after a plant closure, against supply of ~15.5 lakh and demand well above that, which unauthorised brands fill at stations. Ambernath (2 to 3 lakh a day) and Danapur (1 to 2 lakh) should be expanded in FY27; Prayagraj and Mysore have land, Ranchi has confirmation and Bhagalpur needs a better site. Resin costs (preforms, caps) rose with oil after the West Asia crisis and cut the Q1FY27 margin to 9.8%. We assume +4% / +8% / +12% at 11.5-12.5%.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** IRCTC has the strongest position of any listed Indian consumer franchise in its niche: nobody else can sell an online reserved railway ticket. But the moat belongs to the Railways, which granted it, set its price, compete with it for the passenger front-end (RailOne books through IRCTC today) and once ordered half the fee to be shared. The moat protects volume, not pricing power. Catering and Rail Neer are mandates with administered prices; tourism has no moat.

sections.title: Revenue up 5x in eleven years; the margin peaked in FY22 and has fallen every year since

blocks.p: IRCTC's revenue was ₹1,059 cr in FY15 and ₹5,215 cr in FY26. Covid cut FY21 revenue by two-thirds (₹777 cr) because trains and catering stopped; ticketing kept the company profitable. Since FY23 (the first normal year) revenue has grown ~14% a year, but the mix has changed. Catering, which earns a 9-12% segment margin, grew from 42% to 46% of segment revenue, while internet ticketing (80-85% margin) grew only 8-10% a year. So the EBITDA margin has fallen from 46.5% in FY22 (when catering was still partly shut) to 36.0% in FY23, 31.9% in FY26 and 28.2% in Q1FY27. EPS still compounded 11.5% a year over FY23-26 (₹12.57 to ₹17.42), helped by other income on a growing cash pile.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** IRCTC is two businesses in one wrapper. A near-monopoly ticketing platform makes about three-quarters of segment profit on under 30% of revenue; a large, low-margin catering and services business makes most of the growth. Each rupee of new revenue now carries a much lower margin than the average, so EBITDA grows more slowly than revenue (FY26: revenue +11.6%, EBITDA +7.4%) unless the Railways let the ticketing fee rise.

blocks.callout: IRCTC gives no numeric guidance beyond segment growth aspirations, and its management changed between the two calls: the CMD who spoke in May resigned with effect from 20-Jul-2026, and the Director (Tourism & Marketing) now holds the CMD charge. We give most weight to what is visible in the numbers: catering momentum, flat ticketing and margin pressure.

sections.title: Almost no capital needed: ₹4,572 cr of operating cash in six years, ₹520 cr of capex, ~60% paid out

blocks.p: IRCTC runs on other people's assets: the Railways own the trains, licensees run most kitchens and vending, and Rail Neer plants are partly PPP. Net fixed assets were ₹839 cr at Mar-2026 (including an office building and right-of-use assets) against ₹5,215 cr of revenue. Over FY21-26 it generated ₹4,572 cr of operating cash, spent ~₹520 cr on capex and paid out ~₹2,700 cr of dividends; the rest went into bank deposits. Returns are very high (ROE 35-46% since FY22) because equity is small and the ticketing business needs no capital. As a CPSE, IRCTC pays dividends under DIPAM's guidelines and cannot decide a buyback on its own.

blocks.callout: **The capital question:** there is not much of one. Management lists an e-ticketing infrastructure refresh, a disaster-recovery site, two Rail Neer expansions, four new Rail Neer plants and a possible move into hotels (Q4FY26 call); together these are small against ₹1,100-1,300 cr a year of free cash flow. The real lever is the payout: 52% in FY26 under DIPAM rules, with the cash pile still growing.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean cash conversion and small one-offs, but large balances with the Railways

bullets: **Cash conversion is good.** Cash from operations was 91% of net profit in FY26 (₹1,273 cr) and 63% in FY25; working capital absorbs cash as catering grows (receivables ₹1,882 cr, 132 days).

**One-offs are small.** Exceptional items were +₹27 cr (FY23), −₹59 cr (FY24), +₹48 cr (FY25, legacy write-backs) and +₹17 cr (FY26): 1-5% of profit. Q4FY26 also carried a full year of CSR (₹31 cr) and a ₹16 cr ECL provision inside EBITDA. We forecast no exceptional items.

**Other income is real interest.** FY26 other income of ₹260.5 cr was ₹176.0 cr of deposit interest plus ₹84.5 cr of fines and penalties from caterers (₹53.4 cr), deposit amortisation, rent and miscellaneous income. We build FY27E as 6.75% on opening net treasury (₹2,868 cr) = ₹194 cr plus ₹80 cr of other items = ₹{{F.otherIncome.0|num}} cr, against ₹272 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 (before exceptional items).

**Balances with the Railways are large and "subject to reconciliation".** The Railways are customer (receivables), supplier (licence and revenue shares booked gross as expenses) and banker of last resort; Rail Neer profit is shared 15:85 or 40:60 depending on the plant. A reconciliation or policy change can move a year's profit.
**Litigation:** the licence-fee enhancement for prepaid and postpaid trains (CC-60) is sub judice; management would not quantify it.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN.** Unqualified audit (CAG-appointed auditor), no debt, little capex, small one-offs and cash from operations at 91% of profit in FY26 (63% in FY25, when receivables rose). The watch-points are the size of receivables from the Railways and the related-party nature of almost every revenue line, not the accounting itself.

sections.title: No debt, ₹2,868 cr of cash and deposits, and ₹1,882 cr owed by the Railways

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 IRCTC held ₹412 cr in current accounts and ₹2,456 cr in bank deposits and restricted balances (₹149 cr of it margin money against bank guarantees), plus ₹93 cr of accrued interest; its only debt is ₹81 cr of lease liabilities. Net treasury: ~₹2,868 cr, ~₹36 a share, 8% of the market value. The cash is not all free: IRCTC collects ticket and catering money that it owes the Railways (other current liabilities ₹1,524 cr, trade payables ₹930 cr), but it is also owed ₹1,882 cr of receivables (132 days of revenue), mostly by the Railways for prepaid-train catering and services. Working capital is therefore positive and rising with catering. The balances with the Railways are "subject to reconciliation" (AR note 49).

blocks.callout: **Our read:** the government is the controlling shareholder and a regular seller (Oct-2019 IPO, Dec-2020 and Dec-2022 OFS; ~5% more planned in FY27, which would take it to ~57%). It also decides IRCTC's fees, prices and dividends. Retail holders now own more of the free float than foreign funds; an OFS floor price is usually set at a discount to the market.

sections.title: Governance: a clean, well-audited PSU whose owner is also its regulator and main customer

blocks.p: Board: Government-nominated functional directors (CMD, Finance, Catering, Tourism & Marketing) plus government-nominee and independent directors appointed by the Ministry; CMD post held on additional charge since Jul-2026. Rahul Himalian, Director (Tourism & Marketing), holding charge of CMD after Sanjay Kumar Jain's resignation (effective 20-Jul-2026); Rajneesh Narain, Director (Finance) & CFO (Q1FY27 call); Sudhir Kumar signed the FY26 accounts; Manoj Kumar Sharma, Director (Catering Services). Auditor: N.K. Bhargava & Co. (appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor General).

verdicts: N.K. Bhargava & Co. (CAG-appointed); unqualified FY26 opinion (AR FY26).
CMD resigned (personal reasons) with effect from 20-Jul-2026; charge held by a functional director; CFO changed between the May and Aug calls.
Leadership in transition during an OFS year.

Indian Railways is owner, regulator, main customer (receivables ₹1,882 cr) and revenue-share partner (licence fees, Rail Neer profit share 15:85 / 40:60); balances 'subject to reconciliation with the Railways' (AR note 49)
The single biggest governance issue: fees, prices and shares are set by the controlling shareholder.
Oct-2021 order to share 50% of convenience fees, withdrawn within a day; licence-fee dispute (CC-60) in court.
Policy risk is real but has been reversed when it hurt minorities.
Asset-light; pays DIPAM-guided dividends (52% in FY26); cash in bank deposits; buybacks decided by DIPAM
Little capital needed; payout set by DIPAM rules; cash builds up.
No investor presentation; KPIs (tickets, fees, UPI share) given only on calls; segment margins explained in the Q&A.
Analysts asked for a KPI deck twice in 2026.

sections.title: Our forecasts: EPS ₹{{F.eps.0|n1}} / ₹{{F.eps.1|n1}} / ₹{{F.eps.2|n1}}, 2-3% below the street

blocks.p: We forecast each segment's revenue and segment result (as the company reports it, after depreciation) and subtract a small unallocated line to reach EBITDA: catering +19% / +13% / +12% at 10.0-10.5%; ticketing +4% / +6% / +6% at 80-80.5%; tourism +15% / +14% / +12% at 13.5%; Rail Neer +4% / +8% / +12% at 11.5-12.5%. Revenue grows {{F.salesGrowth.0|pct}} / {{F.salesGrowth.1|pct}} / {{F.salesGrowth.2|pct}}, but the EBITDA margin drifts down to {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}} as catering gains share. Capex ₹120-150 cr; depreciation 4% of gross block; other income built from a 6.75% then 6.5% yield on opening net treasury plus ₹80-90 cr of fines, deposit amortisation and rent; tax 25.5%; payout 52%. Every assumption, with our reasoning, is in the Excel model's Assumptions sheet.

sections.title: The street: Buy across the board, targets ₹560-706, multiples cut from 40x to 25-35x this year

blocks.p: All three brokers with a note after the Q1FY27 results rate IRCTC Buy. PL Capital (14-Aug-2026) values it at 35x FY28E EPS (₹706), after cutting its multiple from 40x in May; IDBI Capital (14-Aug-2026) kept ₹610 (method not visible to us); Choice initiated on 22-Sep-2026 at 25x the average of FY28E-29E EPS (₹560), arguing the monopoly "warrants a premium multiple". Median: ₹610, +34% vs the 30-Sep-2026 close of ₹455. Targets have fallen all year: PL ₹850 (Feb) to ₹712 (May) to ₹706; IDBI ₹715 (Feb) to ₹610 (May). The bulls focus on the monopoly, cash and catering growth; the bears on stalled ticketing, the margin and policy risk.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a monopoly at 22.0x Sep-28E EPS; BUY, if the multiple recovers part of its de-rating

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** the Railways' sole online ticket seller (89% of reserved tickets, 80%+ segment margin), its mandated caterer, its water supplier and its pilgrim-train operator. No debt, ~₹2,870 cr of cash and deposits, ROE ~35%, a 52% payout, and growth of ~11% a year in revenue from catering and tourism.

**What you are paying:** 25.2x our FY27E and 22.0x Sep-28E EPS for ~7% a year EPS growth, a fee set by the controlling shareholder and a ~5% government sale still to come. Since 2021 the market has paid a median 42.7x forward for IRCTC. On the street's method and the house multiple the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): BUY. With no sector move it would be ~₹880; with the internet platforms' move alone ~₹450; the DCF says ~₹411.

bullets: **Rating: BUY, target {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}).** Our ratings follow the upside to our 12−month target: BUY at +15% or more, HOLD between −5% and +15%, SELL below −5%.

**This is a multiple call, and we say so.** Our EPS is 2-3% below PL's. The house rule takes IRCTC's own forward P/E median (42.7x) and applies the five-name sector move (−26%): 31.5x. Without a sector move the target would be ~₹880; with the two internet names alone (−48%) ~₹450 (a HOLD); with the railway PSUs alone (−8%) ~₹820.
**We would move to HOLD above ~₹570** and to SELL above ~₹680 on today's numbers, or sooner if ticketing revenue keeps falling in real terms.
**Biggest swing factors:** the multiple (each 1x is ~₹21 a share) and the convenience fee (each 10% is ~5% of EPS).
